Capabilities.description:
Capability metadata advertised on the model catalog.

These fields describe what a model can do rather than how the gateway
reaches it. They are flattened into `[[model]]` and `[[local_model]]`,
validated at load, and surfaced verbatim on `GET /v1/models` so clients
can shape requests before sending them. The effort knobs are chat-only
and require a `thinking` mode other than `never`; the `voices` list is
speech-only.

Whether the model adaptively chooses how much to think per request;
chat kind only. Defaults to false.

default_effort.description:
The effort level applied when the caller omits one; requires a
non-empty `effort_levels` and must name a listed level.

The reasoning-effort levels the model accepts. Empty means the model
has no effort knob.

images.description:
Whether the model accepts image inputs. Defaults to false; a
`[local_model.multimodal_projector]` companion implies true.

max_output.description:
Max output tokens the model can emit per completion. Must not exceed
`context` when set.

parallel_tool_calls.description: Whether the model can emit parallel tool calls. Defaults to false.

The model's provider id, such as `xai`. It describes the model, not

Empty means the model exposes no fixed voice list.

info.description: The Gateway's HTTP API: OpenAI-shaped routes for chat, embeddings, rerank, speech, transcription, and the model list, plus the Gateway's own extensions. Every route follows the standard it is modeled on where one exists, and every addition is named as an extension (`x-runvil-extension`) and is opt-in where the protocol offers a way to ask. Every route except `/health` needs a credential, except that while `[server] trust_loopback` is on, the default, a loopback peer that sends none is admitted; the operations that admit it carry `x-runvil-loopback-trust`.
info.title: Runvil Gateway

post.description:
Two deliberate departures from the other routes. First, auth runs before
body extraction: the handler takes the [`AuthedCaller`] parts extractor,
which runs the auth rules while the parts are extracted, and only then
extracts `WireJson<SpeechRequest>` from the raw [`Request`] by hand, so
an unauthorized caller never makes the gateway parse a body. Second, the
reply is a byte passthrough, not a typed relay: audio frames are opaque
bytes the gateway cannot re-validate per chunk, so the upstream body is
forwarded unread - the one departure from the gateway's typed-relay
norm, the same trade [`crate::relay::relay_sse`] documents for its own
design. Because the response is a long-lived byte stream, this route
must never sit under a `CompressionLayer` or a whole-request
`TimeoutLayer`: both buffer or kill long-lived streams. The stream runs
under the bounded background relay [`relay_audio`] documents, so every
early end - a tripped bound or an upstream failure - fails the client's
body read rather than truncating it.

decoder's prompt are dropped from the end.

always holds one segment for the whole clip and no word timestamps.

A cache hit (blob + sidecar present, pin matching when named) answers
immediately with JSON `{"path", "status": "ready"}`. A miss answers with
`text/event-stream`: `{"status": "downloading", "bytes", "total"}`
progress events (`total` is null when the server sent no Content-Length),
terminated by `{"status": "ready", "path"}` or, on failure,
`{"status": "error", "message"}`.
